pages.text: Mawunyo and her classmate Bright wanted to try a small school enterprise project. ‘Phone cases are always needed,’ said Bright. ‘Let us buy cheaply and sell them here.’ ‘First, let us check that people really want them,’ said Mawunyo.
sentences: Mawunyo and her classmate Bright wanted to try a small school enterprise project.
‘Phone cases are always needed,’ said Bright.
‘Let us buy cheaply and sell them here.’ ‘First, let us check that people really want them,’ said Mawunyo.
pages.alt: Two students talk beside a school desk with an exercise book and a phone.

pages.text: They asked fifteen classmates and neighbours. Eleven said they would buy a case at around 20 cedis, but only two would pay 30 cedis. Mawunyo wrote the numbers in her exercise book.
sentences: They asked fifteen classmates and neighbours.
Eleven said they would buy a case at around 20 cedis, but only two would pay 30 cedis.
Mawunyo wrote the numbers in her exercise book.
pages.alt: The girl writes survey results in a tally table in her exercise book.

pages.text: A trader at the wholesale market sold plain cases for 12 cedis each. With a parent’s help they bought 25 cases: 25 × 12 = 300 cedis. The trotro fare for the trip added 30 cedis. ‘So our real cost is 330 cedis, not 300,’ said Mawunyo.
sentences: A trader at the wholesale market sold plain cases for 12 cedis each.
With a parent’s help they bought 25 cases: 25 × 12 = 300 cedis.
The trotro fare for the trip added 30 cedis.
‘So our real cost is 330 cedis, not 300,’ said Mawunyo.
pages.alt: A trader hands plastic bags of phone cases to the students, with a parent standing nearby.

pages.text: They sold the cases for 20 cedis each. In two weeks they sold 18. Income: 18 × 20 = 360 cedis. ‘We made 360 cedis!’ cheered Bright. ‘Not exactly,’ said Mawunyo. ‘We spent 330. So our profit so far is 360 − 330 = 30 cedis.’
sentences: They sold the cases for 20 cedis each.
In two weeks they sold 18.
Income: 18 × 20 = 360 cedis.
‘We made 360 cedis!’ cheered Bright.
‘Not exactly,’ said Mawunyo.
‘We spent 330.
So our profit so far is 360 − 330 = 30 cedis.’
pages.alt: The students count coins and notes on a desk, with the girl pointing at a sum in her book.

pages.text: Seven cases were left, in a style that had gone out of fashion. ‘We could keep the price,’ said Bright. ‘Or sell them at 15 cedis, which is still more than the 12 cedis each cost us.’
sentences: Seven cases were left, in a style that had gone out of fashion.
‘We could keep the price,’ said Bright.
‘Or sell them at 15 cedis, which is still more than the 12 cedis each cost us.’
pages.alt: A box of seven unsold cases sits between the two students as they think.

pages.text: A girl from JHS 1 asked, ‘Is this case strong?’ Mawunyo told her the truth: ‘It is thin plastic. It protects against scratches, but not hard drops.’ The girl still bought one, and told her friends they were honest.
sentences: A girl from JHS 1 asked, ‘Is this case strong?’ Mawunyo told her the truth: ‘It is thin plastic.
It protects against scratches, but not hard drops.’ The girl still bought one, and told her friends they were honest.
pages.alt: The girl shows a case to a younger student who listens and smiles.

pages.text: They sold the last seven for 15 cedis each: 7 × 15 = 105 cedis. Total income: 360 + 105 = 465 cedis. Total cost: 330 cedis. Profit: 465 − 330 = 135 cedis.
sentences: They sold the last seven for 15 cedis each: 7 × 15 = 105 cedis.
Total income: 360 + 105 = 465 cedis.
Total cost: 330 cedis.
Profit: 465 − 330 = 135 cedis.
pages.alt: A neat page in the exercise book shows sums for total income, cost and profit.

pages.text: They gave 15 cedis to the school library box and shared the remaining 120 cedis: 60 cedis each. Mawunyo also wrote what they had learned: surveys help, real costs include transport, honest answers build trust, and a plan can change. ‘We made money,’ she said, ‘but we also made a better plan for next time.’ The end.

options: Lower the price but stay above cost

activities.definition: The money left after you subtract all your costs from the money you earned.

activities.prompt: Put the steps of the project in order.
items: Ask people if they would buy.
Buy the cases and count the real cost.
Lower the price on the unsold cases and calculate the profit.

activities.prompt: Mawunyo told a customer the truth even though it might lose a sale. When is honesty hard for you, and what helps?

glossary.definition: Money left after subtracting all costs from income.
Money received from selling goods or services.
Selling goods in large amounts, usually to shops or traders.
